task_name: STATIC FOX - Thumbnail and animated channel package
client_brief:
Channel pack time. Six thumbnails, the title animation, and a feed teaser cut from the captures.

The six captures are five seconds each and they are silent, which is fine, because nobody hears the feed anyway. Everything the viewer gets is the text you set on screen. Nobody talks in any of this, so do not put a voice or a caption of a voice on it. A cleared instrumental bed is in the pack as staticfox_bed.wav, and it is the music bed on both teasers.

What we need back

Channel thumbnails: six files, one per upload title, each title exactly as written in the titles file and each built on a moment from the capture that upload title belongs to. Two of the titles are enormous and four are tiny and they still have to look like one channel. Title and mascot fight nothing, including each other, and the title still reads at 320 px wide in a feed.

Animated channel title and end card: one file, wide, six to eight seconds, silent, authored from the identity rather than cut from gameplay. Give the reveal some intent and land on a final frame we can actually use as an end card, with the members line on it complete and all three lines of the end card copy.

Channel feed teaser: one file, wide, twelve to fifteen seconds, music bed. Cut it from at least four of the six captures, with the tagline and the upload line from the end card copy set on screen. No invented footage, and no looping one capture to fill the length.

Channel feed teaser upright cutdown: one file, upright, six to eight seconds, music bed, from the same cut.

Use staticfox_scrap_transparent.png as the supplied mascot artwork, without redesigning or stretching it. Titles, tagline, members line and end card copy all come off the titles file exactly as written.

Use staticfox_bed.wav for both teasers, with no speech or capture audio. The upright teaser uses at least three of the captures used in the wide teaser. Title 1 belongs to capture 01, title 2 to capture 02, and so on through title 6 and capture 06. For capture 04, keep the webcam window whole, cover it fully, or crop it out; do not leave a partly cut face. Use the exact members line and all three end-card lines from staticfox_titles.txt.

Supplied identity artwork
staticfox_scrap_transparent.png is the supplied reusable mascot cutout. staticfox_scrap_render.png and staticfox_patch.jpg are historical references only; mascot extraction and patch reconstruction are not additional deliverables. Preserve the cutout's orange fur, purple headset and silhouette.

What stays fixed
Use the exact titles and end-card copy in staticfox_titles.txt. Match thumbnail titles 1-6 to captures 01-06. Use the supplied Scrap cutout without redesign or stretching. Capture footage keeps its own game colours.

Your design decisions
Choose compelling capture moments, thumbnail composition, reveal timing, motion paths, transitions and the music edit. Build the title animation from identity elements; do not substitute a gameplay montage for it.

Delivery and fonts
Use the placement and export instructions listed with each requested file below. The downloadable OFL fonts in Source assets are the current typefaces for this commission; the typography card gives their roles and weights.

brand_identity.tagline: Co op disasters and bad decisions.
brand_identity.sector: Mid tier comedy gaming YouTube channel: co op gameplay, reaction humour and a weekly members stream.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Running since 2019 out of Manchester, England. One creator with a home setup, six uploads a month plus a Sunday members stream.
brand_identity.about: STATIC FOX is a loud, fast comedy gaming channel built on co op chaos and the creator's on camera reactions. Around four hundred thousand subscribers watch for the disasters, the bad calls and the running jokes. The videos land once people click, so the whole brand fight happens on the thumbnail, in the feed, at a glance.
brand_identity.audience: Mostly fifteen to twenty five, watching in a crowded feed on phones. They want energy and payoff, not taste. Income comes from advertising and channel memberships.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid tier creator funded by ad revenue and memberships. The work has to be loud, saturated and heavy on the face and the moment, because that is what wins the click at this level. Restrained and tasteful reads as the wrong channel; pure noise stops reading as one channel at all. Loud and coherent is the line.

palette.name: Fox Orange
palette.usage: The channel's lead colour, the orange of Scrap's fur in staticfox_scrap_render.png and of the fox-head emblem in staticfox_patch.jpg. In every design it appears in the type, panels, shapes or background, not only inside Scrap: a title fill, Inter type on Jet Black, a solid panel or ground, or a shape.

palette.name: Static Purple
palette.usage: Solid grounds, panels and shapes behind the title and Scrap, echoing Scrap's purple headset. Carries Signal White or Acid Signal type, and is itself an Inter type colour on Signal White. Never a title fill or outline.

palette.name: Acid Signal
palette.usage: Title-word fills, Inter lines on Jet Black or Static Purple, and small highlight shapes. Never a ground or panel; leaving title-word fills aside, no more than 10% of the designed, non-footage area.

palette.name: Jet Black
palette.role: mandatory wherever a title is set
palette.usage: The hard outline on every title word, as the type system requires; also dark grounds and panels, and Inter type on Fox Orange or Signal White grounds.

palette.name: Signal White
palette.usage: Title-word fills, Inter type on Jet Black or Static Purple, and light grounds or panels.

brand_identity.typography: STATIC FOX runs two faces. Step 01, Display / H1, is Anton Regular capitals at 190 px on 200 px leading, tracking -0.01 em, carrying the setup words, for example WE HAD ONE JOB, and dropping to 96 px on long copy. Step 02, Subheading / H2, is the payoff word in Archivo Black Regular at 150 px on 165 px leading, tracking -0.015 em, for example NOPE, set as the last row of that same stack and never condensed. Step 03, Body, is Inter SemiBold 600 at 54 px on 62 px leading, tracking 0, max 65 characters, for tags and the end card. Step 04, Fine print, is Inter SemiBold 600 at 40 px on 52 px leading, tracking +0.03 em, for credits, with merch at 14 pt on 18 pt. Every word of the title carries a hard black outline.
brand_identity.voice: Fast, funny, self deprecating and a bit chaotic, always in on the joke. Example line the brand would write: "We had one job. We did not do the job. New one up now."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: staticfox_scrap_transparent.png is the supplied reusable mascot cutout. staticfox_scrap_render.png and staticfox_patch.jpg are historical references only; mascot extraction and patch reconstruction are not additional deliverables. Preserve the cutout's orange fur, purple headset and silhouette.
brand_identity.values: Repeatability and independence. The creator wants a set that looks like one channel and a file they can keep editing themselves, so they never have to pay for a new one when a title changes.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: A width flip between two supplied faces: step 01 runs the setup capitals in Anton Regular at 190 px and step 02 jumps the final payoff word to Archivo Black Regular at 150 px on the same stack, so a narrow column of capitals fattens hard on the last word. Every word carries the black outline.

type_system.tagline: Co op disasters and bad decisions.

scale.note: Setup words only, all capitals, hard black outline. The whole stack drops to 96 px on long copy.
The payoff word, set as the last row of the same capital stack so the narrow setup suddenly fattens. Never condensed.

scale.sample: We did not do the job. New one up now.

scale.note: Merch prints the same face at 14 pt on 18 pt.

type_system.signature_move: A width flip between two supplied faces: step 01 runs the setup capitals in Anton Regular at 190 px and step 02 jumps the final payoff word to Archivo Black Regular at 150 px on the same stack, so a narrow column of capitals fattens hard on the last word. Every word carries the black outline.
rules: Never set the payoff word condensed.
Every word in the title carries a hard black outline.
On long copy the title stack drops to 96 px rather than breaking the flip.
Loud and coherent is the line: saturated and heavy, but still one channel.
type_system.specimen_note: The samples load the supplied font files. Their display size is reduced for this guide; use the stated deliverable settings, not the on-screen sample size. Fonts and their OFL licences are downloadable in Source assets.
type_system.measurement_notes: Tracking in units means thousandths of an em; 1 pt is 1/72 inch. Pixel settings apply at final exported size. Font size is not cap height.
type_system.application: Apply these roles to newly set text in the requested deliverables. Preserve supplied logo artwork rather than retyping it. Recovered artwork retains its photographed lettering.
type_system.font_access: Use the attached OFL font files at the named weights. These files replace unavailable commercial fonts for this commission. Do not substitute another family or simulate a missing weight.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds and panels are solid Jet Black, Static Purple, Fox Orange or Signal White, and so are shapes, apart from small Acid Signal highlight shapes. Title words (Anton / Archivo Black) are filled Signal White, Acid Signal or Fox Orange, the palette colours that reach 4.5:1 against the hard Jet Black outline every title word carries. Inter lines are Signal White, Acid Signal or Fox Orange on Jet Black; Signal White or Acid Signal on Static Purple; Jet Black or Static Purple on Signal White; Jet Black on Fox Orange, the pairs that reach 4.5:1. Fox Orange appears in the type, panels, shapes or background of every design, not only inside Scrap. Acid Signal is an accent: title fills, Inter lines and small highlight shapes only, never a ground or panel; leaving title-word fills aside, it covers no more than 10% of the designed, non-footage area.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity: no tint, partial transparency, blur, gradient or blend mode on type, outlines, panels or shapes, and no scrim or colour wash of any colour, black and white included, over a capture frame. A hard, unblurred offset shadow or second stroke in a solid palette colour is allowed. In the films, elements may animate position, scale or opacity, with motion blur, while they move; every held frame, and the final end card, is solid and unblurred. A cut or plain fade between shots is a transition, not a tint. Supplied raster identity artwork retains its edge anti-aliasing. Place it at 100% layer opacity; colour rules apply to any intentional recolouring.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, outlines, panels, shapes, icons or backgrounds.
palette_rules.photography: Capture frames keep their own corrected colour and are never recoloured or washed toward the palette; no capture is pushed toward Static Purple #7A2FF2 or any other palette hex. Scrap keeps the orange fur and purple headset drawn in staticfox_scrap_render.png.

creative_scope.fixed: Use the exact titles and end-card copy in staticfox_titles.txt. Match thumbnail titles 1-6 to captures 01-06. Use the supplied Scrap cutout without redesign or stretching. Capture footage keeps its own game colours.
creative_scope.designer_choices: Choose compelling capture moments, thumbnail composition, reveal timing, motion paths, transitions and the music edit. Build the title animation from identity elements; do not substitute a gameplay montage for it.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.
